newsitem.title: INDONESIA: More detained after riot on Indonesia's Java.
newsitem.headline: More detained after riot on Indonesia's Java.

text.p: Indonesia has detained 31 people in the Java town of Pekalongan after recent riots which were apparently sparked by reports a popular singer had switched political allegiances, Antara news agency reported on Friday.

The official news agency quoted Lieutenant-Colonel Soegeng Suryanto, spokesman for the Diponegoro military command which oversees central Java, as saying on Thursday 31 people had been detained and five others were still being sought for allegedly inciting the riots.
Newspapers earlier reported 16 people had been detained after the riots in Pekalongan, a coastal town 300 km (190 miles) east of Jakarta.

Antara said 60 shops were either burned or ransacked, two cars were set ablaze and a state-run bank was damaged during Wednesday's violence in which the rioters mainly attacked the property of ethnic Chinese.
It said eight people were injured during a clash with security officers who tried to disperse the rioters.
"There are no fatalities in the riot," said Suryanto. Antara did not say if the 31 people would be charged.
It was the first violence in Java since a mob attacked Chinese homes and businesses, Christian churches and Buddhist temples in the town of Tasikmalaya in western Java in January.
Four people died in those riots, set off by an incident of police brutality against a Moslem teacher.
Antara earlier quoted army chief General Hartono as describing the violence in Pekalongan as stemming from a singer's apparent switch of political allegiances.

Popular pop singer Rhoma Irama appeared at a ceremony of the ruling Golkar party in Pekalongan on Tuesday along with a high-profile television Islamic preacher and President Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardiyanti Rukmana.
Irama in the past backed the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) but is now listed as a candidate in the country's May 29 poll as a member of Golkar.
Ethnic disturbances between local Dayaks and immigrant Madurese also rocked West Kalimantan province on Borneo island last month. At least 12 people died, military officials and residents said.
The only three parties permitted to contest the elections are Golkar, the PPP and the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).
